"# Slice A, the call — the model of an LLM agent in the language of file 11

## 1. The question, frozen

What is explained: which of the theory's objects an agent built on a large language model instantiates at one call, across calls, only with a record or a harness, and never (W3 section 1). This slice builds the call: what one execution is, what it reads and writes, what organization its carrier text instantiates, what the weights' transport is and what follows from it, what a run of phase 4 can settle, and what a skill file in the context is. Range: agents of the kinds this record has run. Grain: text — what is in the context, what is emitted, and what changes in the emission when the context is changed. Kind of question: mixed, and the mixture matters. A1 to A4 are *what counts as what under this rule* (they fix the objects). A5 and A6 are *what produces it* about the reader's own correspondence. A7 is *what can we tell from what we see*, and it is the part that bounds the others. The model claims no class membership, no creativity, no knowledge, no Deploy for any agent.

## 2. The parts, and the jobs

Ten parts: A1 a call is one execution, delimited by the context read in whole; A2 the adopted coarse physics at the grain of text, with ports as the passages the admitted edits reach; A3 a call realizes one pair and one of possibly several valuations; A4 part of the context is written by the serving stack; A5 the weights' selected transport and its population; A6 the fourth clause of Selected, unknown, and what falls if it fails; A7 what a run settles; A8 a skill file as a carrier and representation as a fidelity fact; A9 relay against construction at a call; A10 the two layers of Part IV at the grain of text.

Jobs: Q3 and Q2 are the owner's, given, and both are shared with slice B — slice A supplies the terms they are stated in and does not answer them. Five jobs are mine, tagged added: state the declared physical input so a judge can check it against Part II; give P4.1's baseline a reason; bound what a run settles; say what a report in the skill's words shows; and say whether Part IV's layers reach this grain. A part held only by an added job is held if that job is real, and A10's is the clearest case: its job came from the slice brief, not from the owner.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Held by, or what would settle it | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 a call is one execution | held, jointly with A2 | Part XII's task sentence with the declared grain | built |
| A2 adopted physics; ports are the passages the edits reach | held | Part X's port sentence (11 only); the edit list is the loose element | built |
| A3 one pair, one of several valuations | held | "Several solutions remain several." (Part II) and the recorded disagreement between two runs of one box | built |
| A4 the serving stack writes part of the context | held if | the claimed source is right and says so | built |
| A5 the weights' selected transport | held if | the fourth clause (A6) and the independence limb | built |
| A6 the fourth clause | unknown | settle the reading; then look in the trainer's record | built |
| A7 what a run settles | held | Derivation 9 with its last sentence | built |
| A8 skill file as carrier; representation | held if | the skill's method written as an organization, then arm (k) | fitted |
| A9 relay is not construction | held | Part X's exclusion | built |
| A10 the two layers at this grain | unknown | the re-identification arm (PA.3); *look inside* cannot bite | built |

The marks are not added up and no count of them is a verdict. Two parts moved in substance from the sketch and one was added because file 11 forced it: A2 (the declared frame is an adopted physics, not a declared input), A8 (the record's evidence read both ways, so no reader is said to represent), and A6 (split out of M2 because it carries its own check and its own consequence).

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** A7 is a derived conclusion — a theorem of file 11 applied — so the flip is not run on it and the proofs test is used instead: drop the premise that the arms share the same inputs and the difference no longer shows two organizations, which is why every arm is handed the same frozen question and document. A5 could have come out the other way: an unbounded training stream with no survival condition fails Selected's third clause. A4 could have come out the other way: the claimed source says some models receive injected passages and others do not.

**Reverse.** Poke the supposed cause — put the skill in the context, or change one of its clauses — and the emission moves: 0 of 16 reports in the method's form without it against 16 of 16 with it (file 54); the flip redirected to the proofs tests in five of six runs under the changed clause (H59). Poke the effect — rewrite the report, or re-mark it with a second marker — and the context does not move. Direction holds at this grain. A7 then says what that buys: an identification, not a production claim, in Part III's words.

**Hunt the answer in the starting points.** The danger is that A2 declares the organization and A3 and A7 read their conclusions off the declaration. Non-circular dependence needs an admitted change that removes a working part and moves the answer: withholding the skill from the context does it, and the record already ran it. The declaration is not doing all the work.

**Add a job.** If the model is right, the same skill text handed to a different reader need not produce the same response to an edit. It did not: under file 30 the DeepSeek reader showed break 2 once in six repeats and the Sonnet reader showed neither break in twelve. That job ruled out the rival "the skill's words fix the report", which is the rival A8 most needs ruled out.

**Build the best rival.** The strongest rival to this slice is: an agent is a function from context to emission, and nothing else is needed. Two changes tell them apart. A3: repeats on one context differ, and a function's outputs do not. A7: two arrangements with the same projection may still differ, and no function of the projection settles that. If repeats never differed and no arm ever differed, the rival and this slice would be one explanation at this level, and the model would say so rather than decide.

**Pairs that pull.** Two real pulls. First, A2 against A4: A2 says the ports are the passages the admitted edits reach, and A4 says passages arrive that the caller cannot edit. A2's port rule gives way to this extent — the injected passages go into the boundary conditions, not the ports — and what would show the line drawn in the wrong place is an arm whose certified field moves with the injected values. Second, inside A7: Part 0 says identical outputs do not make two systems one organization, while Derivation 2 says two candidates no admitted change separates are one account at that grain. Derivation 2 gives way, because phase 4's contract contains input changes and output readings and no change that reaches inside, so (F1) is never checked; agreement is reported as "no separating change on this contract" and never as "one organization".

**Check the patches.** The programme's patches are recorded: W5 qualified M2 and M6 after file 11 changed Derivation 3, and said what it gave up. A6 is a new part, and it is a catch-all in shape — "unknown" can absorb any failure of the provenance claim — so it carries a gauge: a yes-or-no check a trainer's record could answer, and a consequence if the answer is yes (the provenance falls to declared, and every (R) claim in slices B and C falls with it). A part whose failure costs nothing would be a patch; this one costs the rest of the model.

**Look inside.** It cannot bite at this grain: the record shows it ran with content in 3 of 16 reports in one mode and 0 of 16 in the other. The parts it would have settled — whether a reader instantiates a representation (A8), whether it instantiates Part IV's layers (A10) — are left unknown with that test named, never left out.

**What the change list leaves out.** Anything at the grain of weights or activations; the membership of any training history; the exact serving stack of any run in the record; and, for the mode 2 runs already in the record, the context itself, because run.py saves the reply and not the request.

**Where the parts came from.** Eight built, one fitted (A8, written with the record in view), none asserted. The sketch's one asserted part, M1's declared frame, is the one that changed.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Three things, in order. Run arm (k): it is the only test that bears on A8 directly, and A8 is the part the rest of the map leans on. Record the request as sent, per run (PA.1): at present "the context" is an inference from code for every mode 2 run in the record, and A2's ports are unobservable there. Add the re-identification arm (PA.3): it is one edit, it is cheap, and it is the only one of Part IV's three primitive-layer edits that no arm of phase 4 runs.

## 6. What this does not show

Nothing here is a test of the model: every run cited is a run the model was written after reading, and the skill's own rule is that a case a part was fitted on cannot confirm that part. Hard to vary is not true. Nothing here shows that any agent understands, is creative, creates knowledge, or deploys anything; the model names what would have to be shown and no phase here shows it. The claimed sources are claimed: they were read once, on 22 September 2026, at the addresses given, nothing was kept, and a source's use of a word is not the theory's use of it. File 11 is itself under test in the Semantics project's round S76, and every quotation carries its file mark so that what rests on 11 alone can be found again.

## 7. One next step

Before phase 4 writes a line of rig, add to its record the request as sent and the number of requests per run. Three of this slice's parts (A1, A2, A4) turn on what a call actually read, and for the runs already in the record that is not written down anywhere — only reconstructible by re-running the code. It costs one field and it is the difference between a port and an inference."
